  PRACTICE MATERIAL




Driver Assist
Pop Quizzes
6 quizzes — one per course — 10 multiple-choice questions each, 60 questions total.


      How to use these quizzes

      Take one quiz at a time, closed book. Circle your answer for each question. Every question is tagged
      with the module it tests, so a miss points straight back to what to review.

      Target: 9 / 10 before moving on to the next course. If you score below 9, review the missed modules
      and retake the quiz.

      Answer key is separate. No answers appear after the individual quizzes. All answers are grouped in a
      separate Answer Key section at the very back, after a clear page break, so you can print the quizzes
      without the answers.

  Name: ________________________________ Date: ________________ Score: ___ / 10


  Modules Covered

COLLISION AVOIDANCE CAMERA TYPE
1. What does a forward-facing collision avoidance camera primarily detect ahead of the vehicle?
    A. Tire pressure and tread depth
    B. Vehicles, pedestrians, and lane markings
    C. Exhaust gas composition
    D. Brake fluid level

COLLISION AVOIDANCE CAMERA TYPE
2. In a camera-type collision avoidance system, what usually happens first as a collision risk rises?
    A. The airbags deploy
    B. The engine stalls
    C. A visual/audible warning is given, then braking support if needed
    D. The headlights turn off

COLLISION AVOIDANCE CAMERA TYPE
3. Which condition most reduces forward camera collision detection accuracy?
    A. A clean, dry windshield
    B. Dirt, fog, or heavy rain obscuring the camera view
    C. Driving in daylight
    D. Correct tire pressures

LANE DEPARTURE PASSIVE TYPE
4. A passive lane departure system differs from an active system because it:
    A. Steers the vehicle back into the lane automatically
    B. Only warns the driver and does not apply steering correction
    C. Brakes the vehicle to a stop
    D. Changes lanes for the driver

LANE DEPARTURE PASSIVE TYPE
5. How does a passive lane departure system typically alert the driver?
    A. Horn, high beams, and hazard lights
    B. Warning lamp/chime and often steering wheel or seat vibration
    C. Cutting fuel to the engine
    D. Locking the steering wheel




Quiz 1 — Passive Assist Technology                                                                      Page 1 of 2
Quiz 1 — continued
LANE DEPARTURE PASSIVE TYPE
6. A passive lane departure system will normally NOT warn when:
    A. The turn signal is on for an intended lane change
    B. The vehicle is travelling in a straight line
    C. Lane markings are clearly visible
    D. The driver is awake

BLIND SPOT AND CROSS TRAFFIC ALERTS
7. Blind spot monitoring sensors are most commonly located:
    A. In the front grille
    B. On the roof
    C. At the rear bumper corners
    D. Inside the exhaust pipe

BLIND SPOT AND CROSS TRAFFIC ALERTS
8. When a vehicle is detected in the blind spot, the driver is usually warned by:
    A. An indicator in or near the side mirror, often with a chime if signalling
    B. The brake pedal pulsing
    C. The wipers activating
    D. A drop in engine RPM

BLIND SPOT AND CROSS TRAFFIC ALERTS
9. Rear cross traffic alert is most useful when:
    A. Cruising on a highway
    B. Reversing out of a parking space with limited side visibility
    C. Idling at a traffic light
    D. Driving up a steep hill

BLIND SPOT AND CROSS TRAFFIC ALERTS
10. Rear cross traffic alert warns about:
    A. Low engine oil pressure
    B. Vehicles approaching from the left or right behind the vehicle
    C. A flat front tire only
    D. Pedestrians directly in front of the grille
End of Quiz 1. Check your score in the separate Answer Key at the back. Target: 9 / 10.

INTRODUCING ADVANCED DRIVER ASSIST SYSTEMS
1. ADAS features are best described as systems that:
    A. Replace the driver completely on all roads
    B. Assist the driver with sensing, warnings, and partial control tasks
    C. Only control the audio system
    D. Remove the need for driver attention

UNDERSTANDING THE OPERATION PRINCIPLES OF ADAS
2. The basic ADAS operating cycle is:
    A. Charge, discharge, repeat
    B. Sense, process/decide, then warn or act
    C. Heat, cool, lubricate
    D. Start, idle, shut off

ULTRASONIC ADAS SENSORS EXPLAINED
3. Ultrasonic sensors are best suited to:
    A. Long-range highway target tracking
    B. Short-range, low-speed detection such as parking
    C. Reading traffic signs
    D. Measuring exhaust temperature

RADAR TECHNOLOGY IN DEPTH
4. Automotive radar determines a target's speed mainly by using:
    A. The Doppler effect on reflected radio waves
    B. The colour of the target vehicle
    C. Tire rotation speed
    D. Ambient light level




Quiz 2 — Advanced Driver Assist System                                            Page 1 of 2
Quiz 2 — continued
UNDERSTANDING ADAS CAMERA SYSTEMS
5. A key strength of ADAS cameras compared with radar is:
    A. Seeing through dense fog
    B. Classifying what an object is, such as a sign, pedestrian, or lane line
    C. Measuring distance most accurately at long range
    D. Working with the lens fully blocked

AUTOMOTIVE LIDAR EXPLAINED
6. LIDAR builds a 3D view of surroundings by:
    A. Timing reflected laser pulses (time of flight)
    B. Listening for engine sounds
    C. Measuring brake pressure
    D. Reading GPS signals only

PRINCIPLES OF AUTOMATED VEHICLE LOCALIZATION
7. Vehicle localization means determining:
    A. The driver's home address
    B. The vehicle's precise position within its environment/map
    C. The nearest fuel station price
    D. Tire manufacturing location

CONNECTED VEHICLES
8. V2X communication allows a vehicle to exchange information with:
    A. Only its own radio
    B. Other vehicles, infrastructure, and networks
    C. The exhaust system
    D. Manual paper maps

THE AUTONOMOUS VEHICLE BRAIN ADAS AND ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE
9. In an autonomous/ADAS control unit, artificial intelligence is mainly used to:
    A. Inflate the tires
    B. Interpret sensor data, predict behaviour, and support driving decisions
    C. Replace all sensors
    D. Charge the 12V battery

THE AUTONOMOUS VEHICLE BRAIN ADAS AND ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE
10. Sensor fusion means:
    A. Melting sensors together during repair
    B. Combining camera, radar, and other sensor inputs into one reliable picture
    C. Using only one sensor for every task
    D. Turning sensors off at highway speed

End of Quiz 2. Check your score in the separate Answer Key at the back. Target: 9 / 10.

ADAS FRONT CAMERA CALIBRATION
1. Front camera calibration is typically required after:
    A. An oil change
    B. Windshield replacement or camera removal/refit
    C. A tire rotation only
    D. Refuelling

ADAS FRONT CAMERA CALIBRATION
2. Static camera calibration is performed:
    A. While driving at highway speed
    B. Stationary, using targets placed at specified positions
    C. With the camera disconnected
    D. Only at night

ADAS FRONT CAMERA CALIBRATION
3. Before static calibration, the workshop area should be:
    A. Sloped and cluttered
    B. Level, with correct lighting and space for targets
    C. Dark with the vehicle on a lift at full height
    D. Outdoors in heavy rain

ADAS FRONT CAMERA CALIBRATION
4. Dynamic camera calibration differs because it is completed:
    A. On a dynamometer only
    B. During a specified road drive while the system learns lane markings
    C. With the engine off
    D. Without a scan tool connected

ADAS REAR CAMERA AND ALL ROUND VISION CALIBRATION
5. All-round (360-degree) vision systems create a bird's-eye view by:
    A. Using a single roof antenna
    B. Stitching together images from multiple cameras
    C. Using only the rear camera zoomed out
    D. Projecting a hologram




Quiz 3 — ADAS Calibration Guide                                                   Page 1 of 2
Quiz 3 — continued
ADAS REAR CAMERA AND ALL ROUND VISION CALIBRATION
6. If rear camera calibration is incorrect, the most likely symptom is:
    A. Distorted image or parking guide lines that do not match vehicle path
    B. Engine misfire
    C. Low brake fluid warning
    D. Horn failure

ADAS FRONT RADAR CALIBRATION
7. Front radar calibration mainly ensures:
    A. The radar aims correctly relative to the vehicle's thrust line
    B. The radio receives FM stations
    C. The headlights are brighter
    D. Tire balance is correct

ADAS FRONT RADAR CALIBRATION
8. Front radar calibration should be checked after:
    A. Front bumper / radar bracket repair or collision work
    B. Cabin filter replacement
    C. Spark plug replacement
    D. A software-free wash

ADAS FRONT RADAR CALIBRATION
9. A scan tool is used during radar calibration to:
    A. Start the calibration routine and read alignment values / fault codes
    B. Inflate the tires
    C. Bleed the brakes
    D. Program keys only

ADAS FRONT CAMERA CALIBRATION
10. If calibration is skipped after windshield replacement, the lane/forward systems may:
    A. Work better than new
    B. Detect objects offset from their true position or set fault codes
    C. Use less fuel
    D. Disable the wipers permanently
End of Quiz 3. Check your score in the separate Answer Key at the back. Target: 9 / 10.

Quiz 4 — Understanding Stability Control
   Name: ________________________________ Date: ________________ Score: ___ / 10


   Modules Covered

      Stability Control

TRACTION CONTROL
1. Traction control primarily prevents:
    A. Wheel spin during acceleration
    B. Brake pad wear
    C. Steering wheel vibration
    D. Headlight flicker

TRACTION CONTROL
2. Traction control can reduce wheel spin by:
    A. Increasing tire pressure
    B. Braking the spinning wheel and/or reducing engine torque
    C. Opening all windows
    D. Disengaging the clutch permanently

TRACTION CONTROL
3. Traction control detects wheel spin mainly by comparing:
    A. Oil temperature readings
    B. Individual wheel speed sensor signals
    C. Fuel level readings
    D. Mirror positions

STABILITY CONTROL
4. Stability control (ESC) helps the driver by:
    A. Keeping the vehicle heading where the driver steers during a skid
    B. Increasing top speed
    C. Replacing winter tires
    D. Parking the vehicle

STABILITY CONTROL
5. Which sensor is essential for ESC to detect a skid / unwanted rotation?
    A. Rain sensor
    B. Yaw rate sensor
    C. Ambient temperature sensor
    D. Fuel pressure sensor




Quiz 4 — Understanding Stability Control                                           Page 1 of 2
Quiz 4 — continued
STABILITY CONTROL
6. To correct oversteer, ESC will typically:
    A. Brake an individual wheel (often the outer front) to create a correcting yaw moment
    B. Accelerate the rear wheels
    C. Turn the steering for the driver fully
    D. Shut off all brakes

LAUNCH CONTROL SYSTEMS
7. Launch control is designed to provide:
    A. The slowest possible start to save fuel
    B. Fast, repeatable standing starts with controlled RPM and wheel spin
    C. Automatic parking
    D. Hill holding only

LAUNCH CONTROL SYSTEMS
8. During launch control activation, the system typically holds:
    A. Engine RPM at a preset launch limit until the clutch/brake is released
    B. The wipers on high speed
    C. Cabin temperature constant
    D. The fuel cap open

HILL DESCENT
9. Hill descent control helps on steep downhill grades by:
    A. Automatically braking individual wheels to hold a low set speed
    B. Increasing downhill speed
    C. Disengaging all brakes
    D. Raising engine RPM to redline

HILL DESCENT
10. While hill descent is active, the driver can usually adjust target speed with:
    A. The mirror switch
    B. Cruise control speed switches, and override with brake/accelerator
    C. The horn
    D. The headlight switch
End of Quiz 4. Check your score in the separate Answer Key at the back. Target: 9 / 10.

WINDSHIELD WIPER SYSTEMS
1. The wiper park position is controlled so that blades:
    A. Stop in the middle of the windshield
    B. Return to and stop at the base of the windshield when switched off
    C. Keep moving slowly forever
    D. Lift off the glass at speed

RAIN SENSOR TECHNOLOGY
2. A rain sensor detects rain on the windshield mainly by:
    A. Measuring tire grip
    B. Changes in infrared light reflected within the glass
    C. Listening for thunder
    D. Weighing the wiper motor

HEADS UP DISPLAY SYSTEMS
3. A head-up display (HUD) helps the driver by:
    A. Projecting key information in the driver's forward line of sight
    B. Replacing the instrument cluster fuse
    C. Heating the windshield
    D. Dimming all road signs

TIRE PRESSURE MONITORING
4. A direct TPMS system measures tire pressure using:
    A. Wheel speed differences only
    B. A pressure sensor in each wheel/valve
    C. The driver's visual check
    D. Brake temperature




Quiz 5 — Safety and Comfort Systems                                               Page 1 of 2
Quiz 5 — continued
WIRELESS PHONE CHARGING
5. Wireless phone charging in a vehicle works by:
    A. A hidden USB cable
    B. Inductive power transfer from a charging pad to the phone
    C. Solar panels in the seat
    D. The alternator touching the phone

MOBILIZER SYSTEMS
6. An immobilizer (mobilizer) system prevents starting unless:
    A. The headlights are on
    B. A correctly coded key/transponder is recognised
    C. The radio code is entered daily
    D. All doors are open

KEYLESS ENTRY
7. Keyless entry / passive entry allows locking and unlocking when:
    A. The fob is nearby and a door handle sensor/switch is touched or pulled
    B. The key is inserted in the ignition only
    C. The battery is disconnected
    D. The vehicle is moving

KEYLESS ENTRY SYSTEM DIAGNOSIS
8. A keyless entry system fails on one door only. The best first check is:
    A. Replace the engine ECU
    B. That door's handle sensor, wiring, and connector, plus fault codes
    C. Replace all tires
    D. Drain the fuel tank

RADAR CRUISE CONTROL
9. Radar (adaptive) cruise control differs from conventional cruise control because it:
    A. Only works when parked
    B. Automatically adjusts speed to keep a set distance from the vehicle ahead
    C. Removes the brake pedal
    D. Cannot be cancelled by braking

AUTONOMOUS PARKING SYSTEMS
10. An autonomous / self-parking system typically uses ultrasonic sensors to:
    A. Find and measure a suitable parking space, then assist steering into it
    B. Measure engine oil level
    C. Tune the radio
    D. Test the battery

Note: Cruise Control principles are covered within Q9 — conventional cruise holds a set speed only, without distance control. End
of Quiz 5. Target: 9 / 10.

SRS AIRBAG SAFETY
1. Before working on or near SRS components, you should:
    A. Disconnect the battery and wait the manufacturer-specified time
    B. Probe airbag circuits with a test lamp
    C. Keep the ignition on
    D. Short the airbag connector to ground

SRS AIRBAG SAFETY
2. Why must you never use an ohmmeter on a live airbag inflator circuit?
    A. It will flat the vehicle battery
    B. Meter current could deploy the airbag
    C. It will erase fault codes
    D. It will damage the tires

SRS AIRBAG SAFETY
3. An undeployed airbag module should be carried and stored:
    A. With the trim cover facing toward your body
    B. With the trim cover facing away/up, on a clear bench, never stacked
    C. In a hot oven to dry it
    D. Loose in a toolbox with tools

SRS AIRBAG OPERATION
4. The SRS control unit decides to deploy by evaluating signals from:
    A. Crash / acceleration and safing sensors
    B. The radio volume control
    C. The fuel gauge only
    D. The wiper switch

SRS AIRBAG OPERATION
5. The airbag inflates because the inflator:
    A. Uses compressed air from the tires
    B. Rapidly generates gas when ignited by the deployment signal
    C. Is pumped up by the driver
    D. Fills slowly over several minutes




Quiz 6 — SRS Airbag Essentials                                                    Page 1 of 2
Quiz 6 — continued
SRS AIRBAG OPERATION
6. After deployment begins, a frontal airbag inflates fully in approximately:
    A. 5 seconds
    B. Tens of milliseconds
    C. 2 minutes
    D. 1 hour

SRS AIRBAG OPERATION
7. The SRS warning lamp staying on after the bulb check indicates:
    A. Normal operation with no faults
    B. A fault in the SRS system that needs diagnosis
    C. Low fuel
    D. High beam is on

SRS PRE-TENSIONERS
8. A seatbelt pre-tensioner works in a crash to:
    A. Loosen the belt for comfort
    B. Rapidly remove belt slack so the occupant is held firmly
    C. Release the buckle automatically
    D. Adjust belt height

SRS PRE-TENSIONERS
9. Most pre-tensioners are activated by:
    A. The driver pulling a lever
    B. A pyrotechnic charge (or motor) triggered by the SRS control unit
    C. Wind pressure at speed
    D. The seat heater

SRS PRE-TENSIONERS
10. After a crash in which a pre-tensioner fired, the correct action is to:
    A. Reuse it if the belt still clicks
    B. Replace it as a single-use deployed component, following manufacturer procedure
    C. Reset it with a hammer tap
    D. Ignore it and clear codes only

End of Quiz 6. Check your score in the separate Answer Key at the back. Target: 9 / 10.

Answer Key — Quiz 1: Passive Assist Technology
Retake date: ________________ Second score: ___ / 10

1. B — The forward camera detects vehicles, pedestrians, and lane markings ahead.

2. C — Warning comes first; braking support follows if the driver does not respond.

3. B — Dirt, fog, and heavy rain obscure the camera and reduce detection.

4. B — Passive means warn only; active systems add steering correction.

5. B — Lamp/chime plus wheel or seat vibration is the typical passive alert.
6. A — Signalling suppresses the warning for an intended lane change.

7. C — Blind spot radar sensors sit at the rear bumper corners.

8. A — A mirror indicator warns, often with a chime if you signal toward the vehicle.
9. B — Cross traffic alert is designed for reversing out with limited side visibility.

10. B — It warns of vehicles approaching from either side behind you.




Answer Key — Quiz 1                                                                      Separate Key Section
Answer Key — Quiz 2: Advanced Driver Assist System
Retake date: ________________ Second score: ___ / 10

1. B — ADAS assists the driver; it does not remove the need for attention.

2. B — Sense, process/decide, then warn or act is the core ADAS cycle.

3. B — Ultrasonic range is short, ideal for parking and low speeds.
4. A — Radar uses the Doppler shift of reflected radio waves for target speed.

5. B — Cameras classify objects — signs, pedestrians, lane lines — radar cannot.

6. A — LIDAR times laser pulse reflections (time of flight) to build a 3D map.

7. B — Localization is the vehicle's precise position in its environment/map.

8. B — V2X means vehicle-to-everything: vehicles, infrastructure, and networks.

9. B — AI interprets sensor data, predicts behaviour, and supports decisions.

10. B — Sensor fusion combines multiple sensors into one reliable picture.




Answer Key — Quiz 2                                                                Separate Key Section
Answer Key — Quiz 3: ADAS Calibration Guide
Retake date: ________________ Second score: ___ / 10

1. B — Windshield replacement or camera refit changes aim, so calibrate.

2. B — Static calibration is stationary with targets at specified positions.

3. B — A level floor, correct lighting, and target space are required.

4. B — Dynamic calibration completes during a specified road drive.
5. B — All-round vision stitches multiple camera images into a bird's-eye view.

6. A — Wrong rear calibration distorts the image and misplaces guide lines.

7. A — Radar calibration aligns aim to the vehicle's thrust line.
8. A — Bumper, bracket, or collision work can move the radar — check calibration.

9. A — The scan tool starts the routine and reads values and fault codes.

10. B — Skipped calibration can offset detection or set fault codes.




Answer Key — Quiz 3                                                                 Separate Key Section
Answer Key — Quiz 4: Understanding Stability Control
Retake date: ________________ Second score: ___ / 10

1. A — Traction control limits driven wheel spin during acceleration.
2. B — It brakes the spinning wheel and/or reduces engine torque.

3. B — Differing wheel speeds reveal a spinning wheel.

4. A — ESC keeps the vehicle heading where the driver steers in a skid.
5. B — The yaw rate sensor detects unwanted rotation about the vertical axis.

6. A — Braking an individual wheel creates a correcting yaw moment.

7. B — Launch control gives fast, repeatable starts with controlled RPM/spin.

8. A — It holds a preset launch RPM until release.
9. A — Hill descent brakes individual wheels to hold a low set speed downhill.

10. B — Cruise switches adjust target speed; pedals override the system.




Answer Key — Quiz 4                                                              Separate Key Section
Answer Key — Quiz 5: Safety and Comfort Systems
Retake date: ________________ Second score: ___ / 10

1. B — Park control returns blades to the base of the windshield at switch-off.

2. B — Rain sensors use changes in infrared reflection inside the glass.

3. A — HUD projects key information in the forward line of sight.

4. B — Direct TPMS uses a pressure sensor in each wheel.

5. B — Wireless charging transfers power inductively from pad to phone.
6. B — The immobilizer allows starting only with a recognised coded key.

7. A — Passive entry works when the fob is near and the handle is touched/pulled.

8. B — One-door failure points to that handle, wiring, connector, and fault codes.
9. B — Radar cruise keeps a set distance; conventional cruise holds speed only.

10. A — Ultrasonic sensors find/measure the space for assisted parking.




Answer Key — Quiz 5                                                                  Separate Key Section
Answer Key — Quiz 6: SRS Airbag Essentials
Retake date: ________________ Second score: ___ / 10

1. A — Disconnect the battery and wait the specified time before SRS work.

2. B — Ohmmeter current can fire the inflator — never probe it that way.

3. B — Carry/store undeployed modules cover facing away/up, clear and unstacked.
4. A — Crash/acceleration and safing sensor signals drive the deployment decision.

5. B — The inflator rapidly generates gas when ignited.

6. B — Full inflation takes tens of milliseconds.

7. B — A lamp staying on after bulb check means an SRS fault is stored.

8. B — Pre-tensioners remove belt slack instantly in a crash.

9. B — Most are pyrotechnic (some motor-driven), fired by the SRS unit.

10. B — A fired pre-tensioner is single-use — replace per manufacturer procedure.

End of Answer Key. Practice Material — Driver Assist Pop Quizzes, 6 quizzes, 60 questions.
